column1: # settings encyclopedia: windows cloud endpoints (W365 + AVD + Universal Print + servicing).
# Breadcrumb paths pending tenant walk (docs/17 B7).

column8: Defines what a new Cloud PC becomes: join type (Entra vs hybrid) with image and network (Microsoft-hosted vs your ANC) and geography. A wrong policy provisions wrong for every assigned user until fixed.

column7: Intune > Devices > Windows 365 > Azure network connections
column8: Periodic health checks against your vNet (DNS and AD and endpoint reachability). A failed ANC silently blocks new provisioning while existing Cloud PCs keep running: check here first when provisioning hangs.
Per-group toggles: local admin on the Cloud PC and self-service restore with restore-point frequency. Local admin here is the honest answer to most Cloud PC elevation tickets.

Restart and restore (point-in-time) and resize (changes the SKU and needs a matching license) and reprovision (rebuilds from the image: user data on the Cloud PC is gone). Know which is destructive before clicking.

column4: Windows 365 Boot and Switch and Frontline
column8: Boot signs a physical device straight into the Cloud PC (shared-device friendly); Switch task-switches between local and cloud desktops; Frontline shares one license across shift workers with non-dedicated Cloud PCs.

Pooled shares session hosts across users; personal pins one user per host. The validation-environment flag marks the pool that receives service changes first; drain mode stops new sessions on a host for maintenance.
Users get access via app group (Desktop or RemoteApp) which publishes into a workspace the clients subscribe to. Access tickets trace that chain: user to app group to workspace.
Schedule-driven ramp-up and ramp-down of pooled hosts; the AVD service principal needs the power-management role assignment on the subscription or the plan silently does nothing.

column7: Azure portal > AVD > Host pool > RDP Properties
column8: Semicolon-separated string on the host pool controlling redirection (drives and clipboard and cameras) and display behavior (multimon). The string builder answers most "can we block copy-paste" tickets.

column7: Azure portal > AVD > Host pool > Properties
column8: Deallocated session hosts start when a user connects: big cost saver for personal pools; needs the AVD service principal granted VM power rights. Expect a slow first connect while the VM boots.

UDP transport instead of the TCP reverse-connect: direct on managed networks and STUN/TURN over the public internet. Confirm it is actually in use from the client connection details before crediting it for anything.

Media optimization redirects audio and video to the local client (WebRTC redirector service plus the IsWVDEnvironment registry key on the host). Without it every call hairpins through the session host and quality collapses; component versions must be kept paired.

Profiles live in VHDX on a share (VHDLocations or Cloud Cache); antivirus needs the documented exclusions and the FSLogix Apps Operational event log on the session host is where every profile ticket starts.

column4: Session host servicing: agent and stack
column8: The AVD agent auto-updates and the side-by-side stack versions with it; image updates ride the drain-and-replace cycle rather than in-place patching of session hosts. Broker connection issues often trace to a stuck agent update.

Session hosts must reach the documented service FQDNs; the URL validation tool on a host checks them all. Proxy or firewall changes that trim this list produce "no available session host" style mysteries.
Non-native printers reach the service through a connector host; printers then get registered and shared and deployed to devices via Intune policy. Job volume is pooled across the tenant's licenses.

Microsoft blocks feature updates on devices with known compatibility issues; the hold lifts when the issue is fixed. Overriding the hold via policy is possible and usually regretted: check release health for the hold reason instead.
